blindSummary:
This state/province has not typified hate crime at all, per its own LGBT+ welfare sub-director (June 2026). Six LGBT homicides were recorded in the first four and a half months of 2026 alone, including a trans woman found beaten to death in a drainage channel in the state/provincial capital (suspect arrested — a positive institutional response). Two additional deaths in the state/provincial capital in April 2026 were linked by the state/province's attorney general to organised crime. The state/province's own official locates most attacks in one region under armed-group influence, while a civil-society count attributes 102 killings of gay men to named municipalities between 2015–2024.

Activists report victims are no longer attended to and the violence is not acknowledged by the state/province. The arrest in the drainage-channel case is a single positive data point against a backdrop of collective non-acknowledgment. No transfeminicide offence, no hate-crime typification, no investigative protocol.

Well below the national average. Compared with a neighbouring state/province that at least has a gender-identity civil-code reform (2025), this state/province lacks even that; its armed-group amplifier and escalation along the border with another neighbouring state/province make the violence pattern harder to escape. And compared with the leading state/province, where a dedicated unit and mandatory-response protocol exist, this state/province has no legal machinery whatsoever.
